claims.explanation: GSK1070916 is a potent, long-residence-time Aurora B/C inhibitor that kills dividing cells by blocking cytokinesis and inducing polyploidy/apoptosis, so selectivity is driven mainly by how much cells depend on Aurora B/C activity and how readily they undergo mitotic catastrophe rather than by a single lineage. The strongest predictors are high proliferation/mitotic gene expression and intact p53-mediated apoptosis, while functional p53 loss or low mitotic dependency protects lines. TP53 mutation is the most consistent protective feature among the least-affected lines, whereas sensitive lines frequently retain wild-type TP53 and/or carry proliferative drivers such as PIK3CA, KRAS, or MET.

features.basis: TP53-mutant lines are enriched among least-affected lines and p53 loss reduces apoptosis after Aurora B inhibition-induced polyploidy
Aurora B is the primary target; higher AURKB expression increases dependence on its mitotic function
Aurora A is overexpressed/amplified in tumors and contributes to mitotic dependency, though GSK1070916 is >250-fold selective for Aurora B/C
Survivin (BIRC5) is an Aurora B/INCENP complex component and proliferation marker; high expression marks mitotic dependency
High CDK1/mitotic gene expression indicates rapidly dividing cells that require Aurora B for mitosis
Cyclin A2 is a proliferation/mitotic marker; high expression predicts sensitivity to mitotic inhibitors
TOP2A is a proliferation marker co-expressed with mitotic genes and predicts sensitivity to cell-cycle inhibitors
PLK1 is a mitotic kinase; high expression marks mitotic dependency and the virtual cell shows PLK1 downregulation and similarity to BI-2536
PIK3CA mutations are enriched in sensitive gastric/esophageal/ovarian lines and may increase proliferation/Aurora dependency
KRAS mutations appear in several sensitive lines and may drive mitotic/proliferative signaling
MET mutation/amplification in HGC27 may drive proliferation and increase sensitivity to mitotic inhibition
EGFR-mutant lung lines appear in both groups but several are least affected, suggesting EGFR-driven survival signaling may buffer Aurora B inhibition
